outcomes.description: Move the mug so that it is positioned to the right of the headphones.

nodes.question: Are both the mug and the headphones visible enough to compare their positions?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the mug and headphones are identifiable and their relative positions can be judged; fail if the image clearly shows either is absent or the comparison is impossible; unknown if visibility or identification is inconclusive.
nodes.binding: Use only the image to identify the mug and headphones and assess whether their relative placement is observable. This establishes evidence availability, not fulfillment.

nodes.question: Is the mug positioned to the right of the headphones?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the image shows the mug positioned to the right of the headphones; fail if it clearly shows the mug is not to their right; unknown if their relative position cannot be determined. For R1, complete if this check passes; absent if it fails and no requested change has progressed; partial if the mug has moved toward the requested position but is not yet to the right; unknown if required evidence remains unresolved. Unrelated edits do not count as progress.
nodes.binding: Compare the mug’s visible position with the headphones in the image. Judge the requested spatial relationship, without requiring a particular editing technique.

nodes.question: Comparing the source and edited images, what visible evidence indicates whether the mug has moved toward the right of the headphones, and whether a mug is now to their right?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the edited image shows a mug to the right of the headphones. Fail if it clearly shows no mug to their right. In either case, report source-to-edit evidence relevant to progress, such as the source mug's former position, a possible corresponding mug, or a possible additional mug. Do not require proving object identity; unknown only if the relevant positions or evidence cannot be judged.
nodes.binding: Inspect both images and compare the mug(s) and headphones. The source shows a blue mug left of the headphones; the edit may contain multiple mug-like objects and a blurred region near the source location. Describe observable positions and any apparent change, distinguishing direct observation from uncertain correspondence. This check investigates evidence of progress; it does not impose source-object continuity as a condition for satisfying the requested final relation.

nodes.question: Is the mug visibly positioned to the right of the headphones?
nodes.criteria: Use s1 and s2 for visibility and the requested final relation, and s3 for an independent source-to-edit investigation of positions and possible progress. Complete when the requested relation is established by the edited-image endpoint evidence; do not require proof that the edited mug is the same physical mug as in the source. Partial only when support evidence establishes some movement toward the requested relation but does not establish completion. A right-side mug alone establishes the endpoint, not historical movement. Absent only when evidence establishes no requested progress; unknown when necessary evidence is unresolved. Do not treat an ambiguous remnant or uncertain identity as proof of failure or progress.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

response.content: {"accepted":false,"reason":"The fulfillment readout is not reliably composed from the available evidence. s2 can establish that the final relation fails, but its criteria only call the result partial if the mug moved toward the target; s3 can report source-to-edit evidence, yet its pass/fail criteria are based on whether any mug is to the right and do not require a determinate finding of progress or incompleteness. The readout therefore lacks a clear rule for combining a failed endpoint with s3 evidence to distinguish partial from absent, and may leave known progress unresolved. Also, s3 is activated only after s2 pass, fail, or unknown, so it is always active; this is not itself a defect, but its evidence must be composed explicitly. The requested relation and endpoint are otherwise appropriately specified without imposing editing technique or object continuity."}
